title: Saints do not intercede immediately—their petitions rest on Christ’s merit (Bellarmino)
source_text: XLVI. Monent tamen Sanctos non immediate intercedere apud Deum pro nobis, sed eorum intercessionem niti merito Christi, per quem beneficia pro nobis a Deo petunt. Haec enim sunt Bellarmini verba, Sancti non sunt immediati intercessores nostri apud Deum, sed quicquid a Deo nobis impetrant, per Christum impetrant. Lib. 1. de Beatitudine Sanctorum cap. 17. propositione 2.
pass_a_gloss: Yet they warn that the Saints do not immediately intercede before God for us, but that their intercession rests on the merit of Christ, through whom they ask benefits for us from God. For these are Bellarmine’s words: The Saints are not our immediate intercessors before God, but whatever they obtain for us from God, they obtain through Christ. Book 1 on the Beatitude of the Saints, chapter 17, proposition 2.
pass_b_english: Intercession is not immediate: it rests on Christ’s merit.
Bellarmino: Saints obtain from God for us only through Christ.

lemmas.gloss: to rest on / lean on Christ’s merit

choices.why: Bellarmino’s quoted negation of unmediated Saintly pleading.
